/**
 * HomeLog — a personal health diary app. Everything here is patient-generated: the patient (or a
 * device paired to the patient's phone) is the only source. No clinician has reviewed any of it.
 *
 * HomeLog publishes two kinds of item, both using the entry type `HomeLogEntry`:
 *
 * 1. **Day page.** One item per calendar day (on the phone's clock) that has at least one entry.
 *    Published at the first sync after that day ends. Holds that day's BP readings, glucose readings,
 *    dose-log entries and diary notes. The envelope `effective` is the bare date (`2024-10-31`).
 *    If the patient later edits or deletes anything on that day, HomeLog publishes a new day page that
 *    `supersedes` the old one and restates the whole day.
 *
 * 2. **My Medicines list.** One item each time the patient saves their medicine list. Holds one
 *    `my_med` entry per medicine on the list, including ones marked stopped. Each save restates the
 *    whole list and `supersedes` the previous list item. `effective` is the date of the save.
 *
 * Narrative: on a day page, the narrative is the patient's diary notes for the day, verbatim, one
 * paragraph per note. HomeLog adds only the bold time label at the start of each paragraph; the words
 * inside the `<ref>` span are exactly what the patient typed (spelling and all). Readings and dose-log
 * entries have no narrative. A My Medicines list item has a one-line narrative generated by the app
 * ("My Medicines, saved 2 May 2026").
 *
 * Times: HomeLog stores **wall-clock time as shown on the phone, with no UTC offset and no time-zone
 * name** (`"2024-10-31T08:20"`). The app does not know which time zone the phone was in. To place a
 * reading on a timeline you need the patient's time zone from somewhere else. Envelope `recorded`
 * values are server times in UTC and do carry an offset.
 *
 * Medicine names are whatever the patient typed or picked; they are not checked against any
 * prescription. A self-reported list can differ from every clinic's list, and that is the point of it.
 */

/** One entry on a HomeLog day page or My Medicines list. */
export type HomeLogEntry = BpReading | GlucoseReading | DoseLog | DiaryNote | MyMed;

/**
 * Local wall-clock date-time as shown on the patient's phone, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`, no seconds, no
 * offset, no zone. Not UTC. See the module comment.
 */
type LocalDateTime = string;

/** A home blood pressure reading. */
export interface BpReading {
  type: 'bp_reading';

  /** When the cuff took the reading (cuff clock, synced to the phone), or when the patient says it was taken if typed. Local wall time. */
  measured_at: LocalDateTime;

  /** Systolic pressure, mmHg. */
  systolic_mmhg: number;

  /** Diastolic pressure, mmHg. */
  diastolic_mmhg: number;

  /** Pulse rate from the cuff, beats per minute. Absent when typed in and the patient left it blank. */
  pulse_bpm?: number;

  /**

  /** RxNorm ingredient CUI, only when the source states an ingredient-level RxNorm code. Never guessed or derived from a product code. */
  rxnorm_ingredient?: string;
  /** The drug as the source names it (display text), e.g. "losartan potassium 50 MG Oral Tablet" or "Jardiance". */
  drug_name: string;
  /**
   * Status as of `asOf`, by this source's account.
   * - 'active': the patient should be taking it (or, on a patient's own list, says they are).
   * - 'held': paused with intent (or at least possibility) of resuming; the patient should not be
   *   taking it now. Not the same as stopped.
   * - 'stopped': discontinued.
   * - 'unknown': the source lists the drug but records no decision about whether it is being taken
   *   (e.g. a hospital list marked as not reconciled).
   */
  status: 'active' | 'held' | 'stopped' | 'unknown';
  /**
   * Local date on which the current status began according to this source: for 'held' or 'stopped',
   * the date of the hold or stop; for 'active', the date the source's current line or order started
   * (or resumed). Keep the source's precision. Omit if the source does not say.
   */
  status_since?: PartialDate;
  /**
   * Amount per administration currently prescribed (for 'held' and 'stopped': the amount when it was
   * held or stopped). For a patient's own list: the amount the patient says they take, if they give
   * one. `unit` is one of the listed units; convert source spellings ("unit", "UNT", "[iU]" ->
   * "units"; "tab"/"tablets" -> "tablet"). Omit when the source gives no single amount.
   */
  dose?: { value: number; unit: 'mg' | 'mcg' | 'units' | 'mL' | 'tablet' };
  /**
   * How often, normalized: 'QD' once daily, 'BID' twice daily, 'TID' three times daily, 'QHS' once
   * daily at bedtime, 'QW' once weekly, 'PRN' as needed, 'other' anything else. Omit if unknown.
   */
  frequency?: 'QD' | 'BID' | 'TID' | 'QHS' | 'QW' | 'PRN' | 'other';
  /**
   * For 'stopped' rows, why, when the source records a coded or clearly stated reason:
   * - 'adverse_reaction': side effect or adverse reaction.
   * - 'ineffective': not working well enough.
   * - 'therapy_changed': replaced by another drug for the same purpose.
   * - 'course_complete': finite course finished.
   * - 'patient_choice': the patient declined or asked to stop.
   * - 'other': another reason (see `status_reason_text`).
   * Omit when the source gives no reason, and on rows that are not 'stopped'.
   */
  stop_reason?: 'adverse_reaction' | 'ineffective' | 'therapy_changed' | 'course_complete' | 'patient_choice' | 'other';
  /** Free-text reason for the current status (hold or stop) as the source wrote it, if any. */
  status_reason_text?: string;
  /** True when the row comes from the patient's own account (a self-reported list), not a clinician's record. */
  patient_reported: boolean;
  /** True when the source says the drug was bought without a prescription. Omit otherwise. */
  otc?: boolean;
  evidence: Evidence;
}

content.text: Type-check passes. Next I'll run the mapper on the feedback payload to confirm the spironolactone and Jardiance rows.

I've revised `out/transform.ts` to fix the two problems in the feedback. It type-checks, and a test using the feedback patients' medicine entries gives the expected rows. I didn't re-run the other feedback patients (Finerenone, Lisinopril and Kerendia).

- **Held vs. active:** HomeLog has no "paused" status, so patients leave a paused medicine as `taking` and explain in `note`. A `taking` entry whose note says things like "doctor told me to stop for now" is now `held`. The note goes into `status_reason_text`, and `status_since` and `stop_reason` are left out. Stopped entries with pause-style notes still become `held`. Notes that say "permanent" or "never" stay `stopped`.
- **Same drug listed twice:** I changed which entry wins when one ingredient appears more than once, as Jardiance did (one `taking` entry, one `stopped` for DKA). An active entry now beats a stopped one unless the stopped date is clearly later than the active entry's start date. If both are the same kind, the later date wins, as before. This is my reading of the expected "active" result, so it may not match every case in other patients.
